thesis: The cleaner earnings anchor preserves profitability, but bank-specific risk context is missing for both advocates. Neither loan/deposit growth nor the $2.5bn credit-cost level establishes risk-adjusted value without capital, liquidity and asset-quality detail. Neutral avoids interpreting unextracted ratios as deterioration.
strongest_counterexample: Net income excluding significant items was $16.9bn, with average loans up10% and deposits7%, giving a substantial active banking franchise independent of the $21.2bn headline.
invalidation_conditions: A complete comparable bank supplement documents positive ex-significant-item earnings growth, compliance with applicable capital/liquidity requirements and no worsening loan-quality metric, resolving the central bank-risk gates.
A disclosed breach of applicable capital/liquidity requirements or ex-significant-item net income at or below zero would invalidate the retained resilient-franchise premise.
evidence_gaps: CET1, liquidity, funding spreads, detailed losses and risk-adjusted loan returns.
Recurring bank valuation; detailed supplement not fully parsed.
decisive_factors: $2.5bn credit costs cannot be classified without asset-quality context.
Below SMA-50 with negative MACD; oversold RSI is not entry proof.
